note: Feature inventory of PQ-SSE Desktop, checked against the app (app/spatial/copy.py, QML, pqsse/, tests) by scripts/build_feature_inventory.py. Labels are the app's own strings. status: verified = seen in the running app on 2026-11-18 and covered by tests; tested = covered by automated tests, not looked at by hand in this pass; partial = works with a stated gap; not-verified = implemented, never run here.

features.name: Five screens in one window
features.sentence: The window has a dock with five screens: Journey, Stage, Workspace, Security Lab and Insights.
features.produces: Nothing by itself. Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5 (or Alt+1 to Alt+5) switch screens.

features.name: Three roles and the role switcher
features.sentence: Workspace shows the tools of one role at a time: the data owner (the data owner), a receiver (Receiver A, Receiver B or a person you add), or the storage server (Cloud).
features.produces: All three roles run on this one computer, each with its own key store.
limits: All roles run on one PC. There is no setup for separate machines.

features.name: Keys and pairing
features.sentence: Each role creates its own post-quantum keys, locked with a passphrase, and the parties exchange public key files whose fingerprints can be compared by eye.

where.screen: Workspace, Keys card and Join card
labels: Exchange public keys with the cloud

features.produces: An ML-DSA key pair for the data owner; ML-KEM and ML-DSA key pairs for each receiver and for the cloud; .pqpub public key files.
limits: A passphrase cannot be recovered.
Fingerprints are only useful if compared over a path you trust.

features.name: Groups
features.sentence: The data owner sorts documents into groups; each group has its own key, so access to one group gives nothing in another.

where.screen: Workspace, People and access card (More options)

features.produces: A random 32-byte key per group, kept by the data owner.
features.cloud_sees: Group names and that a group exists.

features.name: Documents: add, import, edit, delete
features.sentence: The data owner types a document or imports .txt, .md and .pdf files; the app encrypts each one before it leaves their side, and the owner can edit or delete it later.
features.produces: Each document encrypted with AES-256-GCM and signed by the data owner (ML-DSA).
features.cloud_sees: Encrypted documents, their sizes and how many there are.
limits: PDF import keeps the text only (pypdf); layout and images are dropped.
PDF import was not tried by hand in this pass.

features.name: Join requests and approval
features.sentence: A receiver sends a signed join request; the data owner sees it with the key fingerprint, ticks the groups to allow and approves, and the receiver fetches a sealed access pass.

where.screen: Workspace, Join card (receiver) and People and access card (the data owner)

features.produces: An access pass (capability) with the keys of the chosen groups, sealed for that receiver with ML-KEM and AES-256-GCM and signed by the data owner.
features.cloud_sees: That a request and a sealed pass passed through, their sizes, and which groups the receiver may ask about. Not the group keys.
limits: Across computers the receiver joins with an invite and a one-time code, and both sides compare six fingerprint words.

features.name: Build the index and publish the summary
features.sentence: Uploading documents builds an encrypted index (one masked entry per word, linked in a hash chain), and Publish summary sends a signed, encrypted summary that receivers check every answer against.

labels: Changes are waiting. Receivers do not see them until you publish.

features.produces: Index entries at addresses computed with HMAC-SHA3-256; a summary (state) padded, encrypted, versioned, with an expiry time, signed with ML-DSA.
features.cloud_sees: Addresses and masked values that look random, how many entries there are, the batch size, and the time of each upload.
limits: A summary is valid for a set time (default 24 hours). Inside that time the cloud can still show the newest summary a receiver has already seen.

features.name: Search without unlocking
features.sentence: A receiver types one word; the app turns it into encrypted secret addresses (a token), and the cloud returns what is stored there without learning the word.
features.produces: A list of matching document ids, shown only after Verify passes.
features.cloud_sees: Which addresses were asked for, how many entries matched, when, and whether the same search was made before. Not the word.
limits: One word per search.
The data owner also knows the receiver's cloud pass, so the owner could read the token too.

features.name: Verify every answer: eight checks
features.sentence: Before showing a result, the app runs eight checks on the cloud's answer; if any fails, nothing is shown.

labels: A check failed. No result is shown.

features.produces: The eight checks: state signature, segments complete, older segments final, freshness, no rollback, response signature, completeness, hash chain.
limits: Freshness relies on clocks that roughly agree.

features.name: Open a document
features.sentence: A receiver opens a result; the app checks the data owner's signature on the encrypted document and decrypts it with the group key. Outside the receiver's groups there is no key, so nothing opens.

labels: Pick a result to open it.

features.produces: The document text, on the receiver's side only.
features.cloud_sees: Which encrypted document was fetched, and its size.
limits: Neither policy can take back a document a receiver already opened.

features.name: Update: add and delete with forward and backward privacy
features.sentence: Adding or deleting documents sends a numbered, signed batch; new entries get new addresses an old token cannot reach (forward privacy), and a delete is one more masked entry (backward privacy).
features.produces: A signed update batch with a sequence number; the cloud accepts only the next number.
features.cloud_sees: That an update happened, when, and how large it was. It removes a deleted document's box.
limits: Backward privacy here hides which older entry a delete cancels. The cloud still sees the delete batch and drops the deleted document.

features.name: Revoke: policy R and policy RE
features.sentence: The data owner takes a person's access away; the cloud refuses their pass, each affected group gets a new key, and only the people who stay receive it. Quick (policy R) or Thorough (policy RE).
features.produces: A new key period (epoch) per group, sealed once per remaining receiver. With RE every document is encrypted and signed again.
features.cloud_sees: That a revocation happened, which pass is refused, and with RE the full re-upload.
limits: Policy R: documents from before the change stay under the old key, so a revoked person who teams up with the cloud can still read them.
Policy RE closes that gap but re-encrypts everything.
Cannot be undone.
Known display issue: after a revocation the Stage still lists the revoked receiver's old groups and last search result.

features.name: The local cloud server
features.sentence: The cloud is a separate program on this computer that listens on 127.0.0.1 only; the Cloud role starts and stops it and shows its activity log and what it stores.

where.screen: Workspace as Cloud: Server, Activity log and What it stores cards

features.produces: A cloud database with encrypted documents and index entries; a request log (who asked, which kind of request, how many bytes).
features.cloud_sees: Everything listed on this page under 'What the Cloud sees'. It is never given a group key.
limits: Local demo only: no TLS, no other machine. For other computers use the separate server program (Server program, below).
It ends whenever the app ends.

features.name: Step Inspector
features.sentence: Every real step can be opened in a side panel that replays it slowly at four levels of detail, with Play, Back, Next, Replay and a speed choice.
features.produces: An animation of the step with numbered sub-steps, the real sizes and timings, and which part of the picture is a metaphor.
limits: The animation is slowed down; the note under it gives the real time the operation took.

features.name: Session timeline
features.sentence: The Stage keeps a timeline of every step in this session; clicking a step replays it in the Step Inspector.

labels: This session, step by step. Click a step to replay it.

features.produces: Nothing new; it replays recorded steps.
limits: Kept for the current session only.

features.name: The lens: whose view
features.sentence: On the Stage, the lens shows the same data as each party holds it: Everyone, the data owner sees, a receiver sees, or Cloud sees (the real stored bytes).
features.produces: Nothing new; Cloud sees shows the real stored bytes.

features.name: Story bar
features.sentence: A bar at the top says in one sentence what just happened, and shows whether the cloud is running, which engine is in use, and whether you are in the practice area.
features.produces: Nothing new.

features.name: Command palette and shortcuts
features.sentence: Ctrl+K (or F1) opens a search box that finds screens, roles, lesson steps, settings and glossary words.

labels: Type to find an action, a glossary word, a lesson step or a setting

features.produces: Shortcuts: Ctrl+K and F1 palette, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5 screens, Ctrl+I Step Inspector, Esc closes the inspector.

features.name: Journey: the guided lesson
features.sentence: Thirteen short steps run the whole system for real in a separate practice area, each with Run this step for me, Let me try and Check my work.
features.produces: A practice area with its own data; every passphrase there is the word lesson. Your own data is not touched.
limits: Teaching names (off by default) shows the lesson cast's names, Alice, Bob and Carol, instead of the role names; it changes only what is shown.

features.name: Challenges
features.sentence: Seven short tasks with hints and no score; the app checks each one by what really happened.

labels: Let Receiver B read only Finance
Compare policy R and policy RE

features.produces: A count of challenges done.

features.name: Welcome screen and glossary
features.sentence: The first start shows a welcome screen with the idea, the cast and an honest note; technical words open a one-sentence meaning.

where.screen: First start; glossary words in the Step Inspector and the palette
labels: Words used here (click for the meaning)

features.produces: Nothing new.

features.name: Security Lab: ten attacks
features.sentence: Ten attacks by a cheating cloud or an outsider run for real on a throwaway copy, and each card shows which check stopped it.
features.produces: For each attack: the attacker's action, the check that caught it, and the run's report.
limits: The attacks are the ones the scheme is built to stop. They do not show the leakage the cloud is allowed (sizes, counts, timing, repeated searches).

features.name: Revoking: quick or thorough (R versus RE)
features.sentence: A comparison where a revoked receiver keeps the old key and teams up with the cloud: under policy R older documents stay readable, under policy RE nothing stored can be read.

where.screen: Security Lab, Revoking: quick or thorough

features.produces: How many stored documents the pair can still read under each policy, from a real run.

features.name: Measurements
features.sentence: Insights measures on your computer how long building an index takes on the CPU and on the GPU, and how long each of the ten operations takes, and saves the results as CSV files.
features.produces: Charts and a table of real timings; CSV files.
limits: Numbers are only for the computer they were measured on.
With the default pure-Python ML-DSA, signing dominates the total time.

features.name: GPU engine and self-test
features.sentence: On an NVIDIA GPU the app can compute the index's secret addresses and hash chain in large batches; it uses the GPU only after a self-test shows the results are byte for byte equal to the CPU.

labels: Which engine does the batch work

features.produces: A self-test report and an engine choice. Automatic sends only large batches to the GPU.
limits: Only the GPU build has the GPU engine.
The GPU never runs ML-KEM, ML-DSA, AES-GCM or the cloud.
For small batches the GPU is slower than the CPU.
Tested on one GPU only (RTX 4060 Laptop GPU).

features.name: Settings: theme, motion, text size, mode
features.sentence: Insights sets the theme (Follow Windows, Dark, Light), Reduce motion, the text size up to 200 %, and Beginner or Expert mode.

labels: Expert: technical names and numbers first

features.produces: Saved in settings.json. Expert mode opens the app on Workspace, shows the full run report in the Security Lab and expands Insights.

features.name: Advanced settings: parameter sets, port, validity
features.sentence: Choose the ML-KEM and ML-DSA parameter sets for new keys, the cloud's port on 127.0.0.1, and how long a published summary stays valid.

labels: A published summary stays valid for (hours)

features.produces: ML-KEM-512, 768 or 1024 with ML-DSA-44, 65 or 87. Default: ML-KEM-768 with ML-DSA-65; summary valid 24 hours.
limits: All parties must use the same parameter set.

features.name: Where data is stored and how keys are protected
features.sentence: Everything is kept in one folder per Windows user; secret keys are stored only in key stores encrypted with a key derived from your passphrase.
features.produces: %LOCALAPPDATA%\PQ-SSE-Desktop: owner.sqlite, cloud.sqlite, receiver_<name>.sqlite, pubkeys\, settings.json, logs\ (1 MB, 3 older files kept), and a lesson folder for the practice area. Key stores: scrypt (N = 2^15, r = 8) from the passphrase, then AES-256-GCM per record.
limits: The log never contains passphrases or keys.
The data owner's own readable copies of their documents are saved with the group keys inside their encrypted key store (owner.sqlite), not as plain files.

features.name: The classic window
features.sentence: The earlier six-tab window (Owner, Receiver, Cloud, Attack Lab, Benchmarks, Settings, plus a Learn tab) opens with --classic, or by itself if the new window cannot start.
features.produces: The same functions as the five screens, in tabs.
limits: Kept for compatibility; not restyled.

features.name: Check for updates (only when you click)
features.sentence: In About, Check for updates reads the website's signed file list once, checks its signature, compares versions, and offers the download page or the web installer.

labels: Download and run the web installer
Show Check for updates in About

features.produces: A message: newer version available, newest version, or the reason it could not check.
limits: The app never goes online by itself. A setting hides the button.

features.name: Installers and the portable build
features.sentence: A small web installer picks the Standard or GPU build and checks it; full installers and portable zips are also offered. All install per user without admin rights.

where.screen: Outside the app: the Download page

features.produces: Program folder, Start Menu entry, uninstall entry, optional desktop shortcut. No service and no firewall rule.
limits: Not code signed: Windows shows a SmartScreen warning.
The GPU installer was not install-tested by the script that publishes it.

features.name: Three ways to use it
features.sentence: On first start you choose Local demo (everything on this computer), Data owner or Receiver (the cloud server runs on another computer). Each mode keeps its own data.

where.screen: Welcome sheet; Insights, Mode of use
labels: How will you use this copy?

features.produces: A data folder per mode. The guided lesson always runs on this computer.

features.name: Server program
features.sentence: A separate cloud server for other computers: HTTPS with a pinned certificate, an operator interface on its own machine, limits, backup and restore. As a Windows console program, from Python, or in Docker.

where.screen: Workspace, Cloud server card (Data owner and Receiver modes); pqsse-server on the server

features.produces: A server data folder with the encrypted store, document files, the TLS certificate and the server's keys.
features.cloud_sees: The same as the local cloud. TLS hides the traffic from the network; its key exchange is classical.
limits: Meant for small groups: put a reverse proxy in front of it if it faces the internet.
Not yet tested on separate computers by the author.

features.name: Invites
features.sentence: The data owner makes an invite for one person: a file or link with the server's address and fingerprints, and a one-time code sent another way. The receiver's app checks both keys against it before sending anything.

where.screen: Workspace, Invite a person (Data owner) and Join with an invite (Receiver)

features.produces: A .pqinvite file without the code; a join request that the server accepts once.
features.cloud_sees: The invite's id and expiry, and which invite a request used. Never the code.
limits: Whoever has the file and the code can join once; the data owner still approves after comparing the six words.

features.name: Keys and passphrases
features.sentence: Change a passphrase, back up keys to an encrypted file, restore them on another computer, or lock them now. Keys also lock after 15 idle minutes.
features.produces: A .pqkeys backup file encrypted under its own passphrase.
limits: A forgotten passphrase cannot be recovered.
Locking overwrites the key in memory as far as Python allows; it is not a guarantee.

features.name: Change a person's groups
features.sentence: Give an approved person more groups, or take some away without revoking them. Groups taken away get new keys, so new documents stay out of reach.
features.produces: A sealed grant for the person, or new keys for the groups taken away.
features.cloud_sees: The person's new list of groups.
limits: With R, a person keeps what they could read before the change.

features.name: Activity log
features.sentence: Every data owner action with the server's answer, newest first, checked as a chain so that a removed or changed entry shows.
features.produces: A record kept in the encrypted key file; a CSV file on request (plain text).
limits: A record for the data owner, not evidence for others: the owner holds the key.

features.name: Export, import and recovery
features.sentence: Export a group's documents to one encrypted file and import it elsewhere. After a crash the app finishes what was sent; after restoring an older backup it rebuilds the data owner's state from the server.

where.screen: Workspace, Export or import a group; Recover after restoring a backup

features.produces: A .pqgroup file; a rebuilt group under new keys after recovery.
features.cloud_sees: Recovery copies of group keys and people's records, sealed under a key only the data owner has.
limits: Invites made after a restored backup must be made again.

sees: how many documents and index entries exist
group names, how many receivers there are and which groups each may ask about
when each request happens and how large it is
which addresses a search asks for, so a repeated search is visible
that an update or a revocation happened
never_sees: group keys or any private key

not_included.claim: No deployment across machines: the cloud listens on 127.0.0.1 only, without TLS.
No connection to a real cloud provider.
not_included.evidence: The only server is pqsse/cloud, started as a child process.

not_included.claim: No sync between devices or users' computers.
not_included.evidence: Each role's data is a local SQLite file under %LOCALAPPDATA%\PQ-SSE-Desktop.

not_included.claim: No more than one data owner.
No change of a receiver's groups after approval.
not_included.evidence: README Known limits: no capability update.

not_included.claim: Searches are one word at a time; no phrases or Boolean queries.
The default post-quantum code is pure Python: slow and not constant time.
not_included.evidence: pqsse/pqbackend.py uses kyber-py and dilithium-py unless liboqs is importable; liboqs was never tested here.

mismatches.issue: The revoked receiver is still shown as 'May search: Finance' with the last search result, because the Stage reads the receiver's own stored pass. Seen after the lesson revoked Receiver A with policy R.
The text repeats itself: "the 'hash chain' check in Receiver A's Verify step. DETECTED by the 'hash chain' check."

Describe the classic window (Learn tab, Narrator, toolbar, F1 glossary, 11 Attack Lab demos). In the new window F1 opens the command palette and the Lab has ten attacks plus the R versus RE comparison.
It mentions 'the seven checks'. The app has eight (pqsse/receiver/receiver.py CHECKS).
An unused string still says the polished Journey 'arrives in milestone 5'. Not shown anywhere; can be deleted.

mismatches.where: pqsse/bench.py, Revoke R and Revoke RE rows
mismatches.issue: The labels say 30 documents, but the benchmark adds one document per repeat before revoking, so with 3 repeats the group holds 33. The site quotes the timing without a document count.
